extracted.intended_audience: Principal Investigators, co-PIs, authorized organizational representatives (AORs), sponsored-research officers, and proposal preparers submitting proposals to NSF
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and required content/format for preparing and submitting research and other proposal types to the National Science Foundation (PAPPG Chapter II). Covers required sections, formatting, disclosures, certifications, budget rules, special plans, and submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformance with PAPPG and Grants.gov instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless specified in a program solicitation, all proposals must comply with the proposal preparation instructions contained in Part I of the PAPPG or the NSF Grants.gov Application Guide. Conformance will be strictly enforced unless a written deviation authorization is received in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deviations require advance written authorization from the cognizant NSF Assistant Director/Office Head or designee; such authorizations must be uploaded as a single-copy document and include the name, date, title of NSF official, and nature of deviation. Proposals nonconforming to instructions may be returned without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for reasonable and accessibility accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals with disabilities who need reasonable accommodations as part of the proposal process or to access NSF systems must contact the Office of Equity and Civil Rights (OECR) Disability Program Manager or NSF Section 508 Compliance Officer at least 30 calendar days prior to the proposal deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF may request medical documentation describing impairment and need. Information is confidential. NSF need not provide accommodations that impose undue hardship or fundamentally alter programs. Requests may not include personal use items or extensions to proposal deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF disclosure requirements for senior personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: All senior personnel identified on a proposal must submit disclosure information in the Biographical Sketch, Current and Pending Support, and Collaborators & Other Affiliations documents; these must be accurate, current, and complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations may lead to sanctions (non-acceptance, ineligibility to perform work, suspension/termination, referral to DOJ, placement in FAPIIS/SAM). NSF may require updated Current and Pending Support prior to award and during reporting. NSF may consider factors (harm, intent, pattern, self-disclosure, training, etc.) when determining consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal sections required for a full research proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: A full research proposal must contain: Cover Sheet; Project Summary; Table of Contents; Project Description; References Cited; Budget and Budget Justification; Facilities, Equipment and Other Resources; Senior Personnel Documents (Biographical Sketches, Current and Pending Support, Collaborators & Other Affiliations); Special Information and Supplementary Documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit required sections will result in the proposal not being accepted or being returned without review. Certain proposal types may deviate (see Chapter II.F). All proposals are reviewed using NSF's two merit review criteria (intellectual merit and broader impacts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover Sheet data and required checkboxes
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover Sheet must include requested start date and duration, LOI or preliminary proposal IDs (if applicable), prime organization, organization status, primary place of performance, other federal agencies, and checkboxes for items such as Beginning Investigator, Disclosure of Lobbying Activities, Proprietary Information, Historic Places, Live Vertebrate Animals, Human Subjects, international funding, DURC, Off-Campus Research, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requested duration should be consistent with project complexity; NSF encourages 3–5 year durations when appropriate. Primary place of performance defaults to organization address but must be specified for offsite work. Certain boxes (e.g., Beginning Investigator) apply only to particular directorates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposal must contain a Project Summary not more than one page long consisting of an overview, a statement on intellectual merit, and a statement on broader impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The overview describes the activity if funded and states objectives and methods. The intellectual merit statement describes potential to advance knowledge. The broader impacts statement describes potential societal benefits and desired outcomes. The summary should be informative to peers and, as much as possible, understandable to a broad scientific audience; it should not be an abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Description content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Description must provide a clear statement of work, objectives for the proposed period and expected significance; relationship to current knowledge and PI’s other work; broad plan of work with experimental methods and procedures where appropriate; and must address what, why, how, how success will be measured, and potential benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project activities must be well justified whether using established or innovative methods. The Project Description must include, as a separate section, a labeled 'Broader Impacts' discussion. Plans for data management are described elsewhere (Special Information).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Description page limit and URL prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Project Description (including Results from Prior NSF Support) may not exceed 15 pages; visual materials are included in the limit. URLs must not be used in the Project Description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results from Prior NSF Support portion is limited to five pages. URLs are prohibited because they can circumvent page limits, reviewers are not obliged to view external sites, and external content can change between submission and review. Conformance to page limits will be strictly enforced unless deviation authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Impacts statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Project Description must contain a separate 'Broader Impacts' section describing how the proposed activities may benefit society and contribute to desired societal outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of broader impacts include full participation of underrepresented groups in STEM, improved STEM education, increased public scientific literacy, workforce development, partnerships with industry, improved national security, economic competitiveness, policy-informed science, and enhanced research infrastructure. These examples are not exhaustive or prescriptive; proposers may include other appropriate outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results from Prior NSF Support reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: For any PI or co-PI who has received NSF support with an end date in the past five years or current funding (including no-cost extensions), information on the award must be provided; if multiple awards, report on the one most closely related to the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required information includes: NSF award number, amount and period of support; project title; a summary of the results of the completed work. This helps reviewers assess the quality of prior funded work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal pagination, font, spacing and margin requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use allowable fonts (Arial [not Arial Narrow], Courier New, Palatino Linotype at 10 points or larger; Times New Roman or Computer Modern at 11 points or larger). No more than six lines of text per vertical inch. Margins at least one inch in all directions. Paper size no larger than 8.5 x 11 inches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fonts smaller than specified are allowed only for formulas, figures, tables, captions, or when using Symbol fonts for special characters; readability is paramount. Noncompliance may be grounds for returning the proposal without review. Use standard single-column format; readability should prevent attempts to gain advantage by shrinking text/spacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal page formatting and single-column recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers are strongly encouraged to use only a standard, single-column format for the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard formatting enhances readability. System (Research.gov) automatically paginates uploaded files; uploaded files should omit page numbering unless otherwise directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-copy documents (NSF use only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain categories of information are single-copy documents for 'NSF Use Only' and are not provided to reviewers; these should be submitted in Research.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-copy categories include Authorization to Deviate, List of Suggested Reviewers or Reviewers Not to Include, Proprietary/Privileged Information instructions, and Proposal Certifications provided by the organization. See Chapter II.D and II.E for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization to deviate from proposal preparation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Deviation authorizations (when granted) must be uploaded as a single-copy document and include name, date, title of the NSF official, and the nature of the deviation authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deviations are rare and must be authorized in advance; absent authorization, proposals not following instructions may be returned without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of suggested reviewers or persons to exclude
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers may optionally include suggested reviewers (with contact info and affiliation) or persons they prefer not to review the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These suggestions are optional and considered by the cognizant Program Officer, who may request further information; the Program Officer has discretion to use or ignore suggestions. Exhibit II-2 provides conflict-of-interest information helpful for this list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proprietary or privileged information handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions for submission of proprietary or privileged information are provided in Chapter II.E.1 and in single-copy document guidance; proprietary information submission affects what is disclosed to reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Chapter II.E.1 for procedures. See also chapter references for details about marking and submission. Improperly marked or unjustified proprietary claims may not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: AOR certifications required with proposal submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authorized Organizational Representative must complete required certifications regarding accuracy/completeness of proposal statements and agreement to comply with award terms; certifications include conflict of interest, flood insurance (when applicable), responsible and ethical conduct of research (RECR) training plan, organizational support, compliance with DURC policy, Thornberry Act-related awareness, and safe/inclusive off-campus working environment plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some certifications are government-wide and provided in SAM; NSF-specific certifications must be included. The AOR must ensure only authorized individuals submit proposals. RECR training plan requirement (per COMPETES Act) goes into effect for proposals on or after July 31, 2023; institutions should be prepared to provide plans upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification regarding conflict of interest by AOR
rubrics_metrics.description: AOR must certify that the organization has implemented and enforces a written conflict-of-interest policy consistent with Chapter IX.A, and that required financial disclosures were made and conflicts are/will be managed, reduced, or eliminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicts that cannot be satisfactorily managed must be disclosed via NSF electronic systems. Failure to properly manage conflicts can result in restrictions or other actions described in PAPPG and Chapter IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification regarding Responsible and Ethical Conduct of Research (RECR)
rubrics_metrics.description: AOR must certify that the institution has a plan to provide appropriate training and oversight in RECR to undergraduate students, graduate students, postdocs, faculty, and other senior personnel who will be supported by NSF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although training plans are not required to be included in proposals, institutions should be prepared to provide them upon request. NSF encourages early adoption prior to required date; resources are available (e.g., Online Ethics Center for S&E). RECR requirement addresses mentor training and mentorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification regarding Safe and Inclusive Working Environments for off-campus research
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposals proposing off-campus or off-site research, the AOR must certify that the organization has a plan in place for this proposal regarding safe and inclusive working environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter II.E.9 for additional information. The certification concerns plans addressing harassment, reporting methods, and resolving complaints for off-site activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior personnel certification and Thornberry Act requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior personnel must certify in SciENcv that their Biographical Sketch and Current and Pending Support information are accurate, current, and complete, as required by the William M. (Mac) Thornberry NDAA for FY2021 Section 223(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senior personnel must update Current and Pending Support prior to award and when requested; false representations may be subject to prosecution under various U.S. criminal statutes and civil false claims laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch and Current and Pending Support requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Biographical Sketch(es) and Current and Pending Support documents must be included for senior personnel and require certification of accuracy. These provide disclosures to assist reviewers and program staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Chapter II.D.h(i) and (ii) for format and content. NSF may require updates prior to award. NSPM-33 implementation guidance affects definitions and required disclosures (see footnotes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborators & Other Affiliations disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborators & Other Affiliations information must be submitted to inform reviewer selection and manage conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter II.D.h(iii). Exhibit II-2 contains potentially disqualifying conflicts of interest to guide the content. Accurate disclosures are taken seriously and violations have consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and budget justification content and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposal must include a Budget and Budget Justification detailing salaries and wages (senior personnel, administrative/clerical policy), fringe benefits, equipment, travel (general, domestic, foreign), participant support, other direct costs (materials/supplies, publication, consultants, computer services, subawards, etc.), total direct costs, indirect costs, fees, and amount requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Chapter II.D.2.f and subparts for allowable costs and required detail. Confidential budgetary information procedures are available. Conformance with federal cost principles and NSF policy is required (e.g., 2 CFR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior personnel salary and administrative/clerical salary policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies specify how senior personnel salaries/wages and administrative/clerical salaries/wages should be treated in the budget; administrative/clerical salaries are normally considered indirect and not allowable as direct unless conditions met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See subparts (a) Senior Personnel Salaries & Wages Policy and (b) Administrative and Clerical Salaries & Wages Policy for criteria and allowable circumstances. Procedures and documentation requirements apply; improper charging may be disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel cost rules, including Fly America Act and dependent care
rubrics_metrics.description: Travel costs must follow NSF and federal rules. For international travel, Fly America Act requires use of U.S.-flag air carriers if available. Temporary dependent care costs resulting from travel may be allowable if they meet specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tickets must identify U.S. flag carrier designator code and flight number. Temporary dependent care costs must be a direct result of travel, consistent with recipient’s travel policy, and temporary for the travel period. See 2 CFR §200.475 and Chapter XI.F for additional info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable and unallowable costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The PAPPG lists categories of allowable and unallowable costs (examples include entertainment, meals and coffee breaks, alcoholic beverages, home office workspace, prohibited telecommunications/video surveillance services or equipment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter II.D.2.f(xiii) and related guidance. Specific prohibitions (e.g., certain foreign telecom equipment/services) must be followed. Consult PAPPG and federal regulations for details; inclusion of prohibited costs may lead to disallowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant support costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Participant support costs (stipends, travel allowances, registration fees for participants) have specific treatment in the budget and must be properly identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participant support differs from other direct costs; follow PAPPG instructions on categorization and documentation. Inclusion in Budget Justification meets definition where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subawards and consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: Subawards and consultant (professional service) costs must be listed and justified in the budget and budget justification, and may be provided through any form of legal agreement; substance of relationship matters more than form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide required documentation and justification. See footnote that a subaward may be any form of legal agreement including a contract; include appropriate details in budget and Facilities/Resources sections as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities, Equipment and Other Resources statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Facilities, Equipment and Other Resources section should describe resources available to the project in narrative form and must not include quantifiable financial information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptions may include institutional support but must avoid dollar amounts; resources described here are non-auditable and must not appear in budget/justification as auditable numbers. Chapter II.D.2.g provides preparation guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Information and Supplementary Documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain materials must be provided in Special Information and Supplementary Documentation: Postdoctoral Researcher Mentoring Plan (if applicable), Plans for Data Management and Sharing, rationale for off-campus performance, letters of collaboration, applicable environmental/facility documentation, human subjects/vertebrate animal documentation, and other special components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific instructions for each item are provided in Chapter II.D.2.i and relevant subchapters. Data Management Plan and Postdoc Mentoring Plan have particular content and submission rules; in collaborative proposals a single mentoring plan may suffice for the unified project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdoctoral Researcher Mentoring Plan requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable, proposals must include a Postdoctoral Researcher Mentoring Plan describing mentoring activities for postdoctoral researchers supported by the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain exceptions apply (e.g., when a postdoc is functioning as senior personnel in a supervisory role). For simultaneous collaborative proposals and projects with subawards, one mentoring plan may cover the unified project. Details in Chapter II.D.2.i(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management and Sharing plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers must describe plans for management and sharing of the products of research (data, samples, collections, curriculum materials, other products) in the Special Information and Supplementary Documentation section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans should cover preservation, documentation, and sharing. Data deposit and curation costs may be allowable; see footnotes re: one-time deposit vs curation. Follow Chapter II.D.2.i(ii) for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative and group proposals procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Special submission and documentation procedures apply for collaborative proposals (multiple organizations) and group travel proposals, including required elements of the Project Description and Budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborative proposals may have differing cover sheet and organization-specific requirements; Exhibit and Research.gov provide instructions. Group travel proposals must include statement of need, recent meetings, location/dates, organization/conduct plans, dissemination plans, composition and recruitment plans, and Results from Prior NSF Support (up to five pages). Budget requests for group travel may only request travel costs for the activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposals involving human subjects, live vertebrate animals, or hazardous materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals involving human subjects, live vertebrate animals, hazardous materials, or endangered species require additional supplemental information and determinations as specified in Chapter II.E.4, II.E.5 and other relevant sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental documentation and approvals (IRB, IACUC, biosafety, etc.) may be required prior to award. Follow the specific subchapter instructions for content, format, and submission of required documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposals proposing international activities
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proposal describes international activity, primary countries involved must be listed (enter 'Worldwide' if specific conference location unknown); additional requirements apply for funding foreign organizations or individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International activities include research/training/education in cooperation with international counterparts or virtual cooperation. See Chapter I.E and II.E.8 and footnotes for special cases and additional documentation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe and inclusive conduct and code-of-conduct requirements for conferences/meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: By signing the Cover Sheet for a meeting proposal, the AOR certifies that prior to participation the proposer will assure the meeting organizer has a written policy or code-of-conduct addressing sexual harassment, other forms of harassment, and sexual assault, including reporting and complaint resolution methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposer need not submit the meeting organizer’s policy to NSF, but must assure it exists and addresses complaint mechanisms and resolution for incidents during the meeting. This applies to conferences and workshops supported by NSF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission rules for proposals by former NSF staff
rubrics_metrics.description: For one year after separation from NSF, former employees or IPAs must communicate with NSF through a 'substitute negotiator'; proposals with a former employee as PI/co-PI will not be processed unless a substitute negotiator is designated and documented by the AOR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute negotiator must be from same organization as the PI/co-PI; information should be uploaded as a single-copy document. A co-PI should designate the PI as substitute negotiator where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auto-compliance checks in Research.gov and administrative review recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submission, proposers are strongly recommended to conduct an administrative review to ensure compliance with PAPPG or Grants.gov Application Guide; Research.gov performs auto-compliance checks prior to submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Exhibit II-1 (Proposal Preparation Checklist) to assist the review. The checklist highlights critical items but is not exhaustive. Administrative review helps avoid return without review for nonconformance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marginal note: readability and fairness enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Readability is paramount; adherence to font/spacing/margins is necessary to prevent unfair advantage from compacting content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reader-friendly fonts and sizes; excessive compression of text may be grounds for return without review. The guidelines aim to ensure fairness among proposers.
